layers.title: Present-day rivers
layers.source: Natural Earth 1:10m rivers and lake centerlines
layers.coverage: Major rivers across Turkey. Not a full drainage network.

layers.title: Present-day lakes
layers.coverage: Larger lakes in and beside Turkey, including Van and Tuz. Small lakes are omitted.

layers.title: Approximate paleolakes
layers.source: Roberts 1983, Quaternary Research 19; Wick, Lemcke and Sturm 2003, Quaternary Science Reviews 22
layers.licence: Approximate outlines drawn for this atlas from the published descriptions. Not a reproduced figure.
layers.coverage: Konya basin and a high-stand sketch around Lake Van. Harran canals were not drawn: no open vector was found.

layers.title: Roman roads
layers.source: Itiner-e static version 2024, de Soto et al. 2025, Zenodo
layers.resolution: segment geometries simplified to about 2 km
layers.coverage: Itiner-e roads clipped to about 25.5–45°E, 35.8–42.2°N. Certainty is the dataset field Cons_per_e.
layers.time: Roman, shown with the Classical and Byzantine chip

layers.title: Soil clay, 0–5 cm
layers.resolution: sampled from the 250 m map to about 5 km for this drape
layers.coverage: Turkey window 25.5–45°E, 35.8–42.2°N. Colour is a stretch of the 5th–95th percentile, not a classified map.

layers.title: Soil organic carbon, 0–5 cm
layers.source: SoilGrids 2.0 soil organic carbon mean, 0–5 cm, ISRIC
layers.resolution: sampled from the 250 m map to about 5 km for this drape
layers.coverage: Same Turkey window as the clay layer.

layers.title: Palaeoclimate records
layers.source: NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology
layers.licence: NOAA World Data Service for Paleoclimatology. Open download, no account. Cite the paper and the NOAA file.
layers.resolution: point records; series thinned to at most 280 Holocene samples
layers.coverage: Sofular Cave, Lake Van, and Eski Acıgöl are inside the Turkey window. Soreq Cave (Israel) and Jeita Cave (Lebanon) are regional context and sit south of the map, so they open from the list rather than a pin. Nar Gölü was not in the open NOAA Turkey folders checked on this run.
layers.time: Holocene series, with 8.2 ka and 4.2 ka marks
